messages.author: 806e01faeb19a132
messages.subject: Hadley's Book_alpha within the  Layer() using qplot in ggplot2
parts:
Currently enrolled in a R class that is on the topic of ggplot2. In Hadley's book he speaks about how you can create a layer as an object and store it for later use (Wickham, p. 45). The example uses the following code, which returns this error. I reviewed the index.ggplot2 page and referenced the aesthetic section help information. I am unsure since I am a late adopter to ggplot2 if something has changed. In addition, I referenced the book's website but found no update information concerning this simple task as Hadley suggest. Any information on how to correct this issue. However, if I remove the alpha from the call I can produce the line. Here is the working example: 


bestfit <- geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = F,
                       colour = "steelblue")

qplot(sleep_rem, sleep_total, data = msleep) + bestfit
qplot(awake, brainwt, data = msleep, log = "y") + bestfit
qplot(bodywt, brainwt, data = msleep, log = "xy") + bestfit

This call works. 

The original call from the book and error message: 


> bestfit <- geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = F,
+                        colour =  alpha ("steelblue", 0.5), size = 2)
Error in do.call("layer", list(mapping = mapping, data = data, stat = stat,  : 
  could not find function "alpha"

The book states that the layered grammar shortcut function consist of 
geom_XXX(mapping, data, ..., geom, position), which is familiar to to error in the do.call. So I attempted this: 

 bestfit <- geom_smooth(aes(color = alpha("steelblue",0.5), size = 2),
+                        method = "lm", se = F)
> 
> qplot(sleep_rem, sleep_total, data = msleep) + bestfit
Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : could not find function "alpha"
> 

I am confused. If the you want to create a standalone layer one should be able to produce either a geom or stat through use of the selected arguments. What is  odd about this call is when you move forward to section 4.5 in the book, Hadley explains use of the aes() function by calling the x and y arguments and color. 

Any help would be greatly appreciated.

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Hadley's Book_alpha within the Layer() using qplot in ggplot2
parts:
Hi:

Since the original edition of the book appeared in 2009, several
changes have taken place in the package. For example, certain
functions originally in ggplot2 (circa 2009) were spun off into
satellite packages, notably scales and gtable. In addition, the
theming system was reformulated as of version 0.9.2 in 2012. The error
you're receiving is due to the alpha() function being spun off to the
scales package. Do the following and all should be copacetic:

library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

qplot(sleep_rem, sleep_total, data = msleep) + bestfit
qplot(awake, brainwt, data = msleep, log = "y") + bestfit
qplot(bodywt, brainwt, data = msleep, log = "xy") + bestfit

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Hadley's Book_alpha within the Layer() using qplot in ggplot2
parts:
Winstons book is a bit more up to date.
http://www.cookbook-r.com/Graphs/

Hadley is working on an up to date version as well of the book. 
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2-book

Either one of these would be a better resource than the first book. There's too much that has changed since then. Especially the theming system (function names in particular). Add to that some of the newer things he's been doing with dplyr and tidyr instead of ddply and reshape2 and it's really in need of an update. 

my 2¢ anyway.
